story_title: As Technical Support Staff, I want to reserve available equipment for an event so that the same limited equipment is not committed to incompatible events.

acceptance_criteria.text: Technical Support Staff can reserve available equipment for an event.
The reservation records the equipment type and quantity.
The reservation is associated with the event.
Reserved quantities are no longer considered freely available for overlapping events.
The system prevents reservations exceeding available quantities.
Reservations can be viewed by authorised Technical Support Staff.

open_questions: The reserve feature is not built yet. Steps and results follow the S-25 Equipment request mockup (design/mockups/EquipmentRequests.dc.html), with one simplification the team has confirmed: clicking Reserve always reserves min(requested, available) for that line - there is no quantity box to type into, and Technical Support cannot reserve more than requested or hold back less than what is available. The confirmation, refusal and cancelled-event messages are proposed wording.

Depends on SPM-48: the availability figures and the S-25 page come from SPM-48, which is not yet merged into main. This branch is based on the SPM-48 branch, so the SPM-49 pull request should be raised after SPM-48 is merged (or target the SPM-48 branch).

ANSWERED - who can view reservations (AC6, TC22, TC23): Q&A #66 says Technical Support is not restricted by equipment type or location, and #91 says equipment arrangements are protected: access depends on role and relationship to the event. An Organiser and a Coordinator can already see reservations on their own event's Equipment tab (SPM-47 behaviour, read-only for the Organiser); TC23 checks only that the Technical Support request page is closed to them.

ANSWERED, out of scope - changing or releasing a reservation after it is made: Q&A #114 says requirements may change after reservation, the affected arrangements are reviewed and updated, and Technical Support re-checks suitability and availability; the exact workflow is for the team. That belongs to SPM-50 and the change flow, not SPM-49.

PARTLY ANSWERED - notifying the Coordinator ('the coordinator is notified either way' in the mockup): the briefing lists 'requested equipment is confirmed or found to be unavailable' as a notification, and the Q&A says notifications are BATCHED with configurable frequency, in-app and email, configurable by type. So it is not an instant on-screen effect; it belongs to the notification story and no case is written.

MOSTLY ANSWERED - reserving for a cancelled, postponed, rejected or draft event (TC17): Q&A #68 and #69 and SPM-37 / SPM-38 say cancelling or postponing releases the event's arrangements, so refusing is consistent (and a draft is invisible to Technical Support anyway). Still to confirm: rejected events, and the wording of the refusal message.

ANSWERED in principle - two users reserving the last unit (TC15): Q&A #35 says the system should identify and block overlapping bookings and help prevent double-booking (a hard block, not a warning). The server must therefore check availability again at the moment of saving, not only when the page was opened.

Test data: these cases change the data they read (except TC03, TC22 and TC23). Reseed before running a case again. Their events and items are fixed (Feb to Jul 2027) and must be added to prisma/seed.ts together with these cases.

DECIDED (3 Oct, following the BPMN) - Technical Support sees and reserves equipment only once the event is in Planning (Confirmed: shown, read-only). The SPM-49 test events were moved from 'Under review' to 'Planning' in prisma/seed.ts to match; TC18 updated. Changed in the SPM-50 branch.
